lines.q: Fifty questions, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: in which month does Canada celebrate Thanksgiving?
lines.a: October! On the second Monday, about six weeks before the American one.

lines.q: American Thanksgiving is on which Thursday of November?
lines.a: The fourth! So it can land anywhere from the twenty second to the twenty eighth.

lines.q: Which store's famous parade fills New York City every Thanksgiving morning?
lines.a: Macy's! Millions watch it on the streets and on TV.

lines.q: Which sport fills TV screens every Thanksgiving?
lines.a: American football! The N F L has played on Thanksgiving for about a century.

lines.q: A male turkey is called a what?
lines.a: A tom! Also called a gobbler. Nice, five down!

lines.q: Which red berry sauce is a Thanksgiving classic?
lines.a: Cranberry! Some people still love the can-shaped version.

lines.q: The day after Thanksgiving is a huge shopping day. What is it called?
lines.a: Black Friday! One of the busiest shopping days of the year.

lines.q: Which pie is the classic Thanksgiving dessert?
lines.a: Pumpkin! Spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg and ginger.

lines.q: Every Thanksgiving, what does the American president pardon?
lines.a: A turkey! The lucky bird gets to live out its days on a farm.

lines.q: Which side dish is often topped with marshmallows?
lines.a: Sweet potatoes! Ten easy ones done. How many did you get?

lines.q: Round two, medium. Which Native American people shared the sixteen twenty one harvest feast with the Pilgrims?
lines.a: The Wampanoag! They had lived in that area for thousands of years.

lines.q: In which present-day state was that feast?
lines.a: Massachusetts! On the coast, south of where Boston is today.

lines.q: Which president made Thanksgiving a national holiday in eighteen sixty three?
lines.a: Abraham Lincoln! Right in the middle of the Civil War.

lines.q: Which N F L team started its Thanksgiving home game tradition in nineteen thirty four?
lines.a: The Detroit Lions! The Cowboys joined the tradition in the sixties.

lines.q: What was the Pilgrims' colony called?
lines.a: Plymouth! Great job, fifteen down.

lines.q: Which sitcom had a Thanksgiving episode in every single season?
lines.a: Friends! All ten seasons, including the famous turkey on the head.

lines.q: The song Over the River and Through the Wood was written about which holiday?
lines.a: Thanksgiving! It began as an eighteen forty four poem by Lydia Maria Child.

lines.q: Where do wild turkeys sleep at night?
lines.a: Up in trees! Wild turkeys can fly, and they roost on branches.

lines.q: Which brand runs a famous turkey cooking hotline?
lines.a: Butterball! Its Turkey Talk-Line has helped cooks since nineteen eighty one.

lines.q: Macy's giant parade balloons are filled with which gas?
lines.a: Helium! Medium round done. How's your score?

lines.q: Round three, hard. How many days did the sixteen twenty one feast last?
lines.a: Three days! It was a harvest festival, not one big dinner.

lines.q: In nineteen thirty nine, F D R moved Thanksgiving a week earlier. What did people call it?
lines.a: Franksgiving! He wanted a longer shopping season during the Depression.

lines.q: The turkey bird is native to which continent?
lines.a: North America! Despite the name, it didn't come from the country Turkey.

lines.q: Which Wampanoag man spoke English and helped the Pilgrims?
lines.a: Squanto! He had learned English after being taken to Europe.

lines.q: Who wrote that the turkey was a more respectable bird than the bald eagle?
lines.a: Benjamin Franklin! In a letter to his daughter. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Which state grows the most cranberries?
lines.a: Wisconsin! More than half of America's whole crop.

lines.q: A baby turkey is called a what?
lines.a: A poult! Turkey chicks get their own special name.

lines.q: Why do fresh cranberries float?
lines.a: Air pockets! That's why farmers flood the bogs to harvest them.

lines.q: Which turkeys gobble?
lines.a: Only the males! Hens cluck and yelp instead.

lines.q: What did the Pilgrims sign aboard the Mayflower?
lines.a: The Mayflower Compact! Hard round finished. Still with me?

lines.q: Round four, very hard. About how many Wampanoag men came to the sixteen twenty one feast?
lines.a: About ninety! Almost twice as many as the English settlers.

lines.q: Which president declared the first national day of thanksgiving, in seventeen eighty nine?
lines.a: George Washington! Lincoln made it a yearly holiday much later.

lines.q: Which president was the first to officially pardon a turkey?
lines.a: George H W Bush, in nineteen eighty nine! Truman never actually pardoned one.

lines.q: Which company created green bean casserole?
lines.a: Campbell's! Its test kitchen came up with it in nineteen fifty five.

lines.q: The fleshy flap that hangs over a turkey's beak is called the what?
lines.a: The snood! Thirty five down, nice work.

lines.q: A group of wild turkeys can be called a what?
lines.a: A rafter! Or you can just say a flock.

lines.q: The Three Sisters crops are corn, beans, and what?
lines.a: Squash! The three grow together and help each other.

lines.q: Before sailing to America, the Pilgrims lived for years in which country?
lines.a: The Netherlands! In the city of Leiden, for about eleven years.

lines.q: Which meat did the Wampanoag bring to the sixteen twenty one feast?
lines.a: Deer! Five of them, according to a Pilgrim's letter.

lines.q: Which Arlo Guthrie song is a Thanksgiving radio tradition?
lines.a: Alice's Restaurant! An eighteen minute story song set on Thanksgiving. Very hard round done!

lines.q: Final round, legend! In which year did the Macy's parade begin?
lines.a: Nineteen twenty four! It even had live animals from the Central Park Zoo.

lines.q: Which cartoon star was Macy's first character balloon, in nineteen twenty seven?
lines.a: Felix the Cat! Mickey Mouse didn't fly until the thirties.

lines.q: Which city has America's oldest Thanksgiving parade?
lines.a: Philadelphia! It started in nineteen twenty, four years before Macy's.

lines.q: Sarah Josepha Hale, the mother of Thanksgiving, also wrote which nursery rhyme?
lines.a: Mary Had a Little Lamb! She also campaigned for seventeen years to make Thanksgiving national.

lines.q: In which year did Congress fix Thanksgiving to the fourth Thursday?
lines.a: Nineteen forty one! Right after the Franksgiving mess. Forty five down!

lines.q: From which English port did the Mayflower finally set sail?
lines.a: Plymouth! The same name the Pilgrims later gave their new home.

lines.q: How many passengers sailed on the Mayflower?
lines.a: One hundred and two! Plus a crew of around thirty.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! How many Mayflower passengers survived that first winter?
lines.a: About half! Disease and cold hit them hard.

lines.q: Who led the Wampanoag at the sixteen twenty one feast?
lines.a: Massasoit! His peace treaty with the Pilgrims lasted for decades.

lines.q: Final question. What's the proper name for a turkey's wishbone?
lines.a: The furcula! Make a wish, you made it to the end.
